blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Coquitlam total for condos and townhomes that month.

items.t: Main streets: David Avenue and Coast Meridian Road serve Burke Mountain, with Harper Road off Coast Meridian Road giving primary access to Pinecone Burke Provincial Park.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it does not concentrate as apartment condos at all. The strata listings here are overwhelmingly townhouses in the Smiling Creek and Partington Creek clusters (Mitchell Street, Rocklin Street, Burke Village Promenade, Sheffield Avenue), with apartment form planned, not yet built, at the Burke Mountain Village centre.

Coquitlam community-level context (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, not for Burke Mountain): Condos & Townhomes median sale price $625,000, $687/sqft, sale-to-list 96%, 23 days on market in September 2026.

Transit anchors: there is no SkyTrain station inside Burke Mountain. The nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations are Coquitlam Central, Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas, and Coquitlam Central also has West Coast Express service.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Burke Mountain

items.t: SSMUH as adopted in Coquitlam: up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules.

Watercourse permit area: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 50 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse in Northeast Coquitlam (30 metres in the rest of Coquitlam); Zoning Bylaw s.519 sets flood protection setbacks and s.523 covers riparian areas — a real constraint on creek-edge townhouse complexes' capital planning.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burke Mountain

items.t: The "condos & townhomes" headline number hides the form split. Burke Mountain's 77 September 2026 strata listings are published only in the combined category; on the building evidence in the apartment share of that stock is effectively the village-centre plan, not built buildings — a buyer searching "Burke Mountain condos" is shopping townhouses.

The village centre's library does not exist yet. Library service today is the Coquitlam Public Library Library Link mobile service and the City Centre branch at 1169 Pinetree Way, until the village-centre library in the future community centre opens.

The mountain has been a planned growth area for three decades. Burke Mountain has been defined in City plans as an area for population growth since the early 1990s (Evergreen Line growth areas identified in 1993, further growth areas in 2000–2001), with the Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek and Partington Creek plans created to guide that growth — which is why the stock is uniformly new-plan townhouse and detached form.
The nearest hospital is across the city line. Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border, is the nearest hospital for this area.

Coquitlam rewrote its OCP in 2026. The Interim OCP (Bylaws 5511/5512, adopted April 27, 2026) superseded OCP Bylaw 3479 — feature sheets and older guides citing 3479 for a Burke Mountain property are citing a repealed plan.

Streets, schools and getting around Burke Mountain

items.t: Main roads: David Avenue and Coast Meridian Road serve Burke Mountain, with Harper Road off Coast Meridian Road giving primary access to Pinecone Burke Provincial Park.

Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Smiling Creek and Partington Creek clusters — Mitchell Street, Rocklin Street, Burke Village Promenade, Highland Drive, Monson Crescent and Roxton Avenue — with apartment form planned, not yet built, at the Burke Mountain Village centre.
SnapStats publishes medians at community level only: Coquitlam "Condos & Townhomes" combined median was $625,000 in September 2026 ($687/sqft, 96% sale-to-list, 23 days on market).

Transit: no SkyTrain station is inside Burke Mountain; the nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) stations are Coquitlam Central, Lincoln and Lafarge Lake-Douglas, and Coquitlam Central also has West Coast Express service.
Schools: SD43 catchments are address-based.

Library and care: library service is the Coquitlam Public Library Library Link mobile service and the City Centre branch, 1169 Pinetree Way, until the village-centre library in the future community centre opens; Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the nearest hospital (Fraser Health).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Burke Mountain

items.t: Form B diligence (all 9 counted strata complexes, and both presales once strata-registered): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern.
Fee-simple townhomes (the Roxton Avenue cluster): The Roxton listings make the same point in marketing language: "no strata! YOU OWN YOUR LOT!"

City zoning and plan: Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 governs — small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3, with subdivision minimums of 650 m² and 18.5 m width (R-1, R-3) and 465 m² and 12.5 m width (R-2). The Interim Official Community Plan — Bylaws 5511/5512, 2026 — was adopted April 27, 2026 and supersedes OCP No. 3479; the Burke Mountain neighbourhood plans (Hyde Creek, Smiling Creek, Partington Creek) and the Northwest Burke Vision sit under that framework.

Watercourse check — doubled reach on the mountain: the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area covers all areas within 50 metres of the top of bank of any watercourse in Northeast Coquitlam (30 metres in the rest of Coquitlam); Zoning Bylaw s. 519 sets flood protection setbacks and s. 523 covers riparian areas. Several counted complexes sit between named creeks (Kentwell between Burke Mountain Creek and Smiling Creek; Secret Ridge between two greenbelt creeks; Rocklin on the Creek on a protected creek) — a capital-planning and lot-level check, confirmed per property.

Property tax: City of Coquitlam property tax payment was due July 2, 2026, covering January 1 through December 31, 2026, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants). There is no Vancouver Empty Homes Tax in Coquitlam — that 3% tax is Vancouver only and never applies here.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burke Mountain

items.t: Two projects share the Rocklin name on the same street pair. Rocklin on the Creek (Woodbridge, 2021, 1220 Rocklin Street / 1225 Mitchell Street) and Rocklin (StreetSide, completing 2026, 1295 Rocklin Street) are unrelated projects whose addresses interleave with the Forester and Ballantree Mitchell Street addresses — a Form B or disclosure statement ordered against the wrong Rocklin is this mountain's easiest paperwork error.

The village centre's library does not exist yet: library service today is the Library Link mobile service and the City Centre branch at 1169 Pinetree Way, until the village-centre library in the future community centre opens.

blocks.text: Burke Mountain home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

149 townhomes sold in Burke Mountain with a median price of $1,100,000 (the middle half sold between $955,000 and $1,298,000), taking a median of 14 days to sell at 99.5% of the last list price; 5% sold above list. They had a median $645 per square foot, a median year built of 2023 and a median strata fee of $364 a month.

faq.a: No. Rocklin on the Creek (1220 Rocklin Street, Woodbridge, built 2021, Freehold Strata) is completed stock; Rocklin (1295 Rocklin Street, StreetSide) is under construction with anticipated completions in late 2026. Different builders, different addresses, different diligence (Form B vs disclosure statement).
